title: This Fish Shoots Insects Out of the Air From 9 Feet Away
subject: archerfish

scenes.text: This fish hunts with a water gun, and it never aims where it looks.
The archerfish spits a jet of water and knocks insects off branches from up to three metres away.
Water bends light, so the insect is never where it appears. Yet it hits.
Scientists have observed that it compensates for that bend.
It even shapes the jet: the tongue pushes against a groove in its mouth so trailing water merges into one big blob.
And young fish get better just by watching older ones spit. A sniper that learns by watching.

description:
An archerfish can knock insects off branches with a jet of water from up to three metres away.
Light bends at the surface, so the prey is never where it looks, yet scientists have observed the fish compensating for that. Young fish become more accurate after watching others spit.
